items.stem: Exactly one of the four statements below is true for every nonzero real number $x$. Which statement is true?
items.hint: Write each power out as repeated factors and count the $x$'s; the three exponent laws use three different operations on the exponents.
worked: Product rule: multiplying like bases ADDS the exponents, so $x^{5}\cdot x^{3}=x^{5+3}=x^{8}$.
Power rule: a power raised to a power MULTIPLIES the exponents, so $(x^{5})^{3}=x^{15}$, not $x^{8}$.
Quotient rule: top exponent minus bottom exponent, so $\dfrac{x^{5}}{x^{3}}=x^{5-3}=x^{2}$, not $x^{-2}$.

items.hint: Collapse the numerator into one power of $3$ before you touch the denominator.
The outer exponent lands on every factor inside the bracket, and the bracket says the base is $-2$, not $2$.
worked: Give the outer power to each factor: $(-2x^{3})^{2}=(-2)^{2}(x^{3})^{2}$.
$(-2)^{2}=4$ and, by the power rule, $(x^{3})^{2}=x^{3\cdot 2}=x^{6}$, so that factor is $4x^{6}$.
Product rule with the remaining factor: $4x^{6}\cdot x^{4}=4x^{6+4}$.
